clue.text: Store carrying old copper water regulator

indicators.note: the store holds the next pieces within it, as a bag carries its contents

parts.note: a store or supply of goods is stock
a copper is a police officer, PC for police constable

explanation.surface: A shop holding an antique copper item that controls a water supply.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a synonym: a valve fitted in a pipe to turn the flow of mains supply on or off.

clue.text: A VIP expects to find it in port

definitions.meaning: a very important person, a figure of note

definitions.text: expects to find it in port
definitions.meaning: a drinker expects fortified wine to have a full, weighty texture

explanation.walkthrough: Port here is the wine, not a harbour: body is the fullness of a wine, so one expects some body in port.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a person of importance is called a somebody, as opposed to a nobody.

clue.text: Feathered vertebrate of river and lake

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England (several rivers bear the name)
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird living by a river and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The ouzel is a bird, an old name for the blackbird or the dipper.

clue.text: Alternative design that may not be needed?

definitions.text: Alternative design that may not be needed?

parts.words: Alternative design that may not be needed?
parts.note: a backup scheme drawn up in advance, kept in reserve in case the main one fails

explanation.definitionFit: A fallback arrangement prepared for an eventuality is exactly a scheme held in reserve for emergencies.

clue.text: Outcry about beauty being robbed of grand

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the word for beauty loses something stolen from it, here a single letter

parts.note: glamour is alluring beauty
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A public protest over a beauty queen stripped of a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being robbed of' takes the G from GLAMOUR, leaving LAMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a loud, insistent public protest or uproar.

clue.text: Fuss about a fighter's leisurely movement

indicators.note: the word for fuss goes around the following pieces

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
a GI is an American soldier, a fighter

explanation.surface: Commotion over a soldier's slow dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a movement played slowly and at ease takes this tempo marking as its name.

clue.text: Fail in aspiration, as a Cockney?

definitions.text: Fail in aspiration, as a Cockney?

parts.words: Fail in aspiration, as a Cockney?
parts.note: aspiration in phonetics is sounding an h; a Cockney Londoner famously leaves the h off words like 'house'

explanation.walkthrough: Aspiration looks like ambition, but in speech it is the breathy h sound. A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner whose accent omits it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to leave out the h sound in speaking, as a Cockney accent does.

clue.text: State university team involved in sports festival

indicators.note: the university and the jumbled team sit inside the festival

parts.note: a gala is a sports meeting, as in a swimming gala

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of team are jumbled

explanation.surface: A national university team takes part in an athletics meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a US state but means a nation. 'involved' rearranges the team's letters, and 'in' places them, with U, inside the festival word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American country, a state in the sense of a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Leading cricketer's device for get ting at drink

definitions.meaning: one of the two batsmen who start a cricket innings

definitions.text: device for get ting at drink
definitions.meaning: a tool for removing caps from bottles or lids from cans

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsmen who go in first are the openers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the batsman who begins the innings, and a bottle or tin gadget.

clue.text: Way a virtuous person accommodates elder, perhaps

indicators.note: the saint makes room for the tree inside it

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a virtuous person
the elder is an example of a tree, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A good person takes in an older relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder' looks like an older person but is the tree, flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a road or thoroughfare in a town is a way.

clue.text: Two close relatives, one called Perry?

parts.note: ma is mother, a close relative
a son is another close relative

explanation.surface: A mother and child, and someone named Perry.
explanation.walkthrough: Perry Mason is the fictional defence lawyer of Erle Stanley Gardner's novels and the TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the famous fictional lawyer bearing the first name Perry has this surname.

clue.text: When able to, turned out carrying right navigational aid

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the right inside them
turned out means rearranged, so the letters of able to are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone, once capable, set off with the correct instrument for finding the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges ABLE TO into TOLABE, and 'carrying' puts R inside, making TROLABE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old instrument used by sailors to measure the altitude of stars and so fix position.

clue.text: Pugnacious bachelor taking girl round Greek island

indicators.note: the girl's name goes around the island

parts.note: Ellie is a girl's name
Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A belligerent single man takes a girlfriend on a tour of an island in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: eager to fight, warlike and aggressive.

clue.text: Honour directions, getting well-upholstered

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
S and E are compass directions, south and east

explanation.surface: Being honoured with instructions on how to get comfortably furnished.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-upholstered is a jokey euphemism for plump, carrying much extra weight.

clue.text: Provide punt for wealthy widow

parts.note: to do can mean to provide, as in 'we do lunches'
a punt is a bet, especially in British slang

explanation.surface: Lay on a flat-bottomed boat for a rich widow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests the river boat, but here it is a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow who holds a title or property from her late husband, typically a grand elderly lady.

clue.text: Tray one's left with daughter carrying tiny plant

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Tray one's left with daughter carrying tiny plant': WATER needs WAITER less I, but 'Tray one' cannot give WAITER and 'one' would do two jobs; likely garbled OCR, no scan or source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Tray one's left with daughter carrying tiny plant

clue.text: Ancient citizen entertaining governor in West End bar

indicators.note: the outer pieces host the governor inside them
End picks the last letter of West

parts.note: to ban is to bar
HE is His Excellency, the style of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: An old-time resident hosting a governor in a London theatre-district pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like the London theatre district, but it is the end letter of West.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Thebes, the ancient Greek (or Egyptian) city.

clue.text: Prevail upon agent that's brought up kid, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent

indicators.note: say signals that the sound of the word is what counts

parts.note: kid is soft leather from young goats, like suede

explanation.surface: Coax a representative who has raised a young goat, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns REP into PER; 'say' makes SUEDE sound as SUADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to prevail upon someone is to talk them round, convince them.

clue.text: Lines initially stigmatising greater part of African state

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of stigmatising
most of the country's name is kept and its last three letters dropped

parts.note: Tanzania is a country in East Africa

explanation.surface: Verses shaming most of an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greater part of' cuts TANZANIA down to TANZA.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Zealous medic given rise in a hospital department.

indicators.note: the reversed doctor sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

indicators.note: in a down clue the medic is lifted, read upwards

parts.note: DR abbreviates doctor

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic doctor promoted within a clinic's department.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: passionate and fervent in enthusiasm.

clue.text: Travesty as Norwegian king for gets lines in church

indicators.note: the shortened king goes inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: forgets means leaves out, so a letter is dropped from the king's name

parts.note: Harald is the name of several Norwegian kings, including the present one
L stands for line

explanation.surface: A farce in which a Norwegian monarch forgets his lines in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for gets' is 'forgets' split by the printing; it drops the line letter from the king's name. Harald V is Norway's present king.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an absurd pretence, a mockery of the real thing.

clue.text: Arrive without favourite to take part in race?

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word for arrive surrounds the favourite

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Turn up without the favourite to run in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to take part in a contest is to vie with others, the question mark as a race is one example.

clue.text: Blunder beginning to ruffle the chief electrician

parts.note: a gaffe is a blunder

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of ruffle

explanation.surface: A mistake starts to upset the head electrician.
explanation.definitionFit: On a film or TV set the head of the lighting crew holds this job title.

clue.text: Rich clothing a bishop always dis plays

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A bishop forever shows off his fine vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: Array is an old word for splendid attire, as in 'battle array'.

clue.text: US politician, oddly, is true lover of the Bard

parts.note: Dem is short for a Democrat

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters of is true are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American politician is, strangely, a faithful Shakespearean romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges IS TRUE into ETRIUS. 'oddly' may suggest alternate letters, but they would not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: one of the young lovers in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Country girl enters fashionable area

indicators.note: the girl's name goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A rural girl walks into a trendy district.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation of South Asia, the world's most populous.

clue.text: Medieval mercenary. rejecting shelter in country

indicators.note: the reversed shelter goes inside the country

parts.note: France is a country

indicators.note: rejecting turns the word back, read backwards

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A hired soldier of the Middle Ages turns down a refuge in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a free lance was a knight-for-hire who sold his services to any lord.

clue.text: Monster Hercules slew in lengthy drama

indicators.note: the letters sit within the two words lengthy drama

explanation.surface: A creature killed by Hercules in a long play.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-headed serpent of Lerna, killed as one of the hero's twelve labours.

clue.text: I would enter arena on horse

indicators.note: the contraction goes inside the arena

parts.note: a ring is an arena, as in a circus or boxing ring
I'd is short for I would

explanation.surface: I would go into the ring on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mounted on a horse means one is out in the saddle, hacking along.

clue.text: Fellow soldier creates chaos and leaves

parts.note: to mess is to make a mess, create chaos
mate is a South American tea brewed from leaves

explanation.surface: A comrade in arms makes a mess and walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the leaves of maté, a herbal drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Messmates share a mess, the dining area of soldiers or sailors.
